title: Blue Earth, MN
description:
Paul Bunyan Paul Bunyan Paul Bunyan.

That was all I was talking to Canek about and it was just making him more angry. I had recently (4 hours ago) disconnected his bluetooth because he was blasting Future in small town Wisconsin, and he was still pissed about it. I was doing what my Mom would always do when my brother and I had road trip beef, which was to refocus our attention on the next Thing that was interesting enough to be in the rest stop brochures. Canek and I both love the movie Fargo, so my thought process at the time was that he felt the same excitement I did to see the Paul Bunyan statues in Minnesota. We were going to pull into a small town with one and eat casserole off the dash and get to the bottom of why Marge Gunderson is kinda hot.

I think my mind was drawn to Marge Gunderson that day because, in addition to being attractive, she has that authenticity, that same small town midwestern pureness, that Canek had ruined for me earlier that morning.

Unknown to me at the time, the south part of Minnesota that I-90 passes through is more like North Iowastan. It has all the flatness, cornfields, and highway hypnosis of the blander parts of the midwest, and, unfortunately, none of the lakes, flannels, and, yes, Paul Bunyan statues that I was expecting. Instead, in an ecological sneak diss, the world’s largest Jolly Green Giant statue stands tall in Blue Earth, Minnesota, staring down its lumberjack enemies to the north.

Not quite as folksy as Paul, but isn’t comparison the thief of joy? And authenticity is doing what you can with what you have. So, I let Canek play Fuck Up Some Commas in the statue parking lot while I got out and took pictures, and both of us were happy.
